context: Al-Ma'idah is among the last surahs to come down, from the years of treaties, settled authority and the Farewell Pilgrimage. The community it addresses is no longer improvising: it has borders, agreements with other powers, and the ordinary business of a state, and the surah opens accordingly with a command to fulfil contracts.

It carries the verse the community understood immediately as a closing: this day I have perfected your religion for you. Umar is reported to have wept when he heard it, because a thing that is completed has nothing further to come. It was revealed at Arafah during the Farewell Pilgrimage, and the Prophet ﷺ died some months later.
name_story: Named for the ma'idah, the table spread with food that the disciples of Isa asked to be sent down from heaven as a sign. The story sits near the end of the surah and is characteristic of it: a request for a sign is granted, and comes attached to a warning that a sign refused after being given is worse than one never asked for.

movements.note: The opening command, then the lawful and unlawful in food, purification, and the covenant taken from the community.
The covenants of Bani Israil and of the Christians, the two sons of Adam, and the verse on the sanctity of a single life.
The relationship of the three scriptures, the command to judge between them by what Allah revealed, and warnings against taking as allies those who mock the religion.

movements.h: Do not make unlawful what is good
movements.note: Against inventing prohibitions, then oaths, intoxicants and gambling, game while in ihram, and the law of bequest.
The table from heaven, and the exchange in which Isa is asked whether he told people to take him and his mother as gods, and answers that he said only what he was commanded.

themes.t: A contract is a religious obligation
themes.d: The surah opens on fulfilling agreements and returns to oaths and covenants repeatedly, treating a broken word as a matter of faith rather than of manners.

themes.t: Justice owed to people you dislike
themes.d: Do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just. Be just; that is nearer to righteousness. The verse assumes the hatred is real and rules on it anyway.
The verse of perfection closes the legislative project, and much of the surah reads like a final tidying of loose obligations.
A distinct warning against forbidding the good things Allah has made lawful, aimed at a piety that expresses itself by adding restrictions.

heart: Recited slowly, the surah's refrain of covenant begins to feel like a handshake tightening. Being Muslim is presented here as a promise already accepted and now waiting to be kept, and the reciter is repeatedly asked whether the specific agreements of his own week, the contract, the oath, the debt, the marriage, are being honoured with the seriousness the surah assumes.

Its hardest instruction for most readers is the one about justice toward people you dislike. It does not ask you to stop disliking them. It fixes your conduct while the dislike remains, which is a far more usable command than an instruction to feel differently.

passages.why: This day I have perfected your religion for you. Revealed at Arafah on the Farewell Pilgrimage; Umar is reported to have wept because completion means nothing more is coming.
Do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just. The most demanding sentence in the surah.
Whoever saves one life, it is as if he saved humanity entirely. Stated as something prescribed to Bani Israil, and carried forward.
Do not make unlawful the good things Allah has made lawful for you. A correction aimed at excess rather than at laxity.

connections.why: Both are long Madinan legislations, and Al-Ma'idah closes much of what Al-Baqarah opened.
The two together carry most of the family and civic law of the Qur'an.

virtue.text: No authentic report establishes a specific merit for reciting Al-Ma'idah. Its standing rests on its content and its timing: it carries the verse of the perfection of the religion, revealed at Arafah in the final year, which the community recognised at once as a closing.
